subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Writers' and Actors' Strike
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Writers' and Actors' Strike usable.

hook.text: In 2023, Hollywood writers and actors went on strike simultaneously for the first time in over 60 years.

buildup.text: Writers were being paid less for streaming shows than for network TV. Residuals had nearly disappeared.

discovery.text: Studios used data secrecy as a weapon.

twist.text: AI became a flashpoint. Writers demanded protections against studios using artificial intelligence to replace them.

climax.text: After 148 days, the strike ended with new residual rules and AI guardrails. Labor fought technology and won—for now.

punchline.text: Streaming made billions but tried to pay writers less.

quiz.question: What was a major issue in the 2023 Hollywood writers' strike?
options: Fair residuals from streaming and AI protections
